jurisdictions.title: Iowa (US-IA)
jurisdictions.statusLine: Restricted. You may not stand *in a roadway* to solicit a ride from a private driver. Iowa's statute expressly protects soliciting a ride from the part of the highway "not ordinarily used for vehicular traffic." Being a pedestrian anywhere on a fully controlled-access highway is illegal.

sections.summary:
Iowa has one of the clearest hitchhiking statutes in the country. Iowa Code § 321.331(1) bans standing in the roadway to solicit a ride from the driver of a private vehicle. Subsection 2 then states that nothing in the traffic code prevents a pedestrian from standing on the part of the highway "not ordinarily used for vehicular traffic" to solicit a ride. In plain terms, hitchhiking from the shoulder is expressly lawful.

What applies to hitchhikers:

- **Stand on the shoulder, not in a lane.** The statute protects you there.
- **Stay off interstates and other fully controlled-access highways completely.** Section 321.366(1)(g) makes it unlawful to "be a pedestrian, anywhere" on such a facility. Drivers also may not stop on the shoulders or right-of-way except at rest areas or in an emergency. Wait on the surface road before the on-ramp, or at a truck stop.
- **Walk on the left side of the highway** (§ 321.326).

The scheduled fine for soliciting a ride from the roadway is $35. Being a pedestrian on a controlled-access highway carries a $135 scheduled fine.
sections.laws:
### Iowa Code § 321.331: Pedestrians soliciting rides

**Source:** [Iowa Legislature, Iowa Code 2026, § 321.331](https://www.legis.iowa.gov/docs/code/321.331.pdf)

> 1. No person shall stand in a roadway for the purpose of soliciting a ride from the driver of any private vehicle.
> 2. Nothing in this section or this chapter shall be construed so as to prevent any pedestrian from standing on that portion of the highway or roadway, not ordinarily used for vehicular traffic, for the purpose of soliciting a ride from the driver of any vehicle.

**What it means:** Don't stand in a traffic lane to hitch. Iowa law expressly says you may stand on the part of the road not ordinarily used by traffic, such as the shoulder, to ask for a ride. This is a statutory green light for shoulder hitchhiking, but it does not override the controlled-access ban below.

### Iowa Code § 321.1: Definitions

**Source:** [Iowa Legislature, Iowa Code 2026, § 321.1](https://www.legis.iowa.gov/docs/code/321.1.pdf)

> 65. "Roadway" means that portion of a highway improved, designed, or ordinarily used for vehicular travel.
>
> [...]
>
> 78. "Street" or "highway" means the entire width between property lines of every way or place of whatever nature when any part thereof is open to the use of the public, as a matter of right, for purposes of vehicular traffic.

**What it means:** The roadway is the travel lanes. The highway is the whole public right-of-way. Section 321.331(2) settles the question for hitchhikers by protecting the part "not ordinarily used for vehicular traffic."

### Iowa Code § 321.366: Acts prohibited on fully controlled-access facilities

**Source:** [Iowa Legislature, Iowa Code 2026, § 321.366](https://www.legis.iowa.gov/docs/code/321.366.pdf) (last amended 2024 Acts, ch 1137, §6)

> 1. It is unlawful for a person, except a person operating highway maintenance equipment or an authorized emergency vehicle, to do any of the following on a fully controlled-access facility:
> [...]
> f. Stop, park, or leave standing a vehicle, whether attended or unattended, upon the shoulders, or the right-of-way except at designated rest areas or in case of an emergency or other dire necessity.
> g. Ride a bicycle or use a pedestrian conveyance, or be a pedestrian, anywhere on a fully controlled-access facility.
> 2. For the purpose of this section, "fully controlled-access facility" is a highway which gives preference to through traffic by providing access connections at interchanges with selected public roads only and by prohibiting crossings at grade or direct access at driveway connections.
> 3. Violations of this section are punishable as a scheduled violation under section 805.8A, subsection 6.

**What it means:** Don't set foot on an interstate or similar freeway, ramps and shoulders included ("anywhere"). A driver who stops on a freeway shoulder to pick you up is also breaking the law. Rest areas are the exception for stopping, but as a pedestrian you are still "on" the facility there, so it's safer to hitch from the surface road before the ramp.

### Iowa Code § 321.326: Pedestrians on left

**Source:** [Iowa Legislature, Iowa Code 2026, § 321.326](https://www.legis.iowa.gov/docs/code/321.326.pdf)

> Pedestrians shall at all times when walking on or along a highway, walk on the left side of such highway.

**What it means:** When walking along a road, stay on the left, facing oncoming traffic.

### Iowa Code § 805.8A: Motor vehicle and transportation scheduled violations

**Source:** [Iowa Legislature, Iowa Code 2026, § 805.8A](https://www.legis.iowa.gov/docs/code/805.8A.pdf)

> 6. Operating violations. For operating violations under the following sections, the scheduled fine is as follows:
> [...]
> y. Section 321.366 ........................................ $135.
>
> 9. Bicycle or pedestrian violations. For bicycle or pedestrian violations under the following sections, the scheduled fine for a pedestrian or bicyclist is as follows:
> [...]
> h. Section 321.331........................................ $ 35.

**What it means:** Hitching from a traffic lane carries a $35 scheduled fine. Walking on an interstate carries a $135 scheduled fine. Court costs and surcharges are added to both.

jurisdictions.title: Kansas (US-KS)
jurisdictions.statusLine: Restricted. You may not stand *in a roadway* to solicit a ride. The roadway excludes the berm and shoulder, so thumbing from the shoulder or curb is not covered by this rule. Hitchhiking and walking anywhere on the Kansas Turnpike are banned by regulation, and drivers may not stop there to pick up hitchhikers.

sections.summary:
Kansas has the Uniform Vehicle Code rule, K.S.A. 8-1538(a): "No person shall stand in a roadway for the purpose of soliciting a ride." "Roadway" is defined as "exclusive of the berm or shoulder". Hitchhiking from the shoulder or curb of an ordinary road is not prohibited by this statute.

What applies to hitchhikers:

- **Stay out of the travel lanes.** Soliciting a ride from the roadway is a traffic infraction. The uniform fine schedule lists $45, plus court costs.
- **Never hitchhike on the Kansas Turnpike** (the toll road run by the Kansas Turnpike Authority). Turnpike regulations ban pedestrians entirely and ban "solicitation of rides, commonly known as hitchhiking, on any portion of the turnpike." Drivers are also forbidden to stop to pick up or drop off hitchhikers on the turnpike.
- **Other interstates and freeways:** KDOT or local authorities may ban classes of traffic, such as pedestrians, from controlled-access highways. The ban applies where official signs are posted. Disobeying those signs is a misdemeanor.
- **Walk on the sidewalk** if there is one, otherwise on the shoulder. With neither, walk on the left edge facing traffic.
sections.laws:
### K.S.A. 8-1538: Soliciting rides, business or contributions; exception

**Source:** [Kansas Office of Revisor of Statutes, K.S.A. 8-1538](https://www.ksrevisor.gov/statutes/chapters/ch08/008_015_0038.html) (official; history: L. 1974, ch. 33, § 8-1538; L. 1995, ch. 65, § 1)

> (a) No person shall stand in a roadway for the purpose of soliciting a ride.
>
> (b) No person shall stand on a highway for the purpose of soliciting employment, business or contributions from the occupant of any vehicle.
>
> (c) No person shall stand on or in proximity to a street or highway for the purpose of soliciting the watching or guarding of any vehicle while parked or about to be parked on a street or highway.
>
> (d) The soliciting of contributions under subsection (b) shall not be prohibited, if such person or organization has first obtained a permit authorizing such soliciting from the local authorities in their respective jurisdictions.

**What it means:** Subsection (a) covers rides and is limited to the roadway. Subsection (b) covers employment, business and contributions, and uses the wider word "highway", which includes the shoulder. A hitchhiker is soliciting a ride, so (a) is the rule that applies. Thumbing from the shoulder is outside it. Don't offer to pay for or work for a ride with a sign that could be read as "business".

### K.S.A. 8-1459 and 8-1424: "Roadway" and "Highway" defined

**Source:** [K.S.A. 8-1459](https://www.ksrevisor.gov/statutes/chapters/ch08/008_014_0059.html) and [K.S.A. 8-1424](https://www.ksrevisor.gov/statutes/chapters/ch08/008_014_0024.html)

> 8-1459. "Roadway" means that portion of a highway improved, designed, or ordinarily used for vehicular travel, exclusive of the berm or shoulder. In the event a highway includes two (2) or more separate roadways the term "roadway" as used herein shall refer to any such roadway separately but not to all such roadways collectively.
>
> 8-1424. "Highway" means the entire width between the boundary lines of every way publicly maintained when any part thereof is open to the use of the public for purposes of vehicular travel.

**What it means:** The shoulder is part of the "highway" but not the "roadway". The ride rule in 8-1538(a) stops at the edge of the travel lanes.

### K.S.A. 8-1537: Pedestrians; use of roadways

**Source:** [K.S.A. 8-1537](https://www.ksrevisor.gov/statutes/chapters/ch08/008_015_0037.html)

> (a) Where a sidewalk is provided and its use is practicable, it shall be unlawful for any pedestrian to walk along and upon an adjacent roadway.
>
> (b) Where a sidewalk is not available, any pedestrian walking along and upon a highway shall walk only on a shoulder, as far as practicable from the edge of the roadway.
>
> (c) Where neither a sidewalk nor a shoulder is available, any pedestrian walking along and upon a highway shall walk as near as practicable to an outside edge of the roadway, and, if on a two-way roadway, shall walk only on the left side of the roadway.

**What it means:** Use the sidewalk. If there isn't one, use the shoulder. If there's no shoulder, walk on the left edge facing traffic.

### K.S.A. 8-1525: Regulation and restrictions on use of controlled-access highways and facilities; misdemeanor

**Source:** [K.S.A. 8-1525](https://www.ksrevisor.gov/statutes/chapters/ch08/008_015_0025.html)

> (a) The secretary of transportation, by duly adopted resolution or order, and local authorities by ordinance or resolution, may regulate or prohibit the use of any controlled-access highway or facility within their respective jurisdictions by any class or kind of traffic which is found to be incompatible with the normal and safe movement of traffic.
>
> (b) The secretary or the local authority adopting any such prohibition shall erect and maintain official traffic-control devices on the controlled-access highway or facility on which such prohibitions are applicable, and when in place no person shall disobey the restrictions stated on such devices. Violation of this subsection (b) is a misdemeanor.

**What it means:** On free interstates and freeways, a pedestrian ban applies where it is signed. Ignoring a posted ban is a misdemeanor (see 8-2116 below), which is more serious than the $45 infraction for soliciting from the roadway.

### K.A.R. 39-1-1 and 39-1-2: Kansas Turnpike, prohibited users; hitchhiking and loitering

**Source:** [K.A.R. 39-1-1](https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/kansas/K-A-R-39-1-1) and [K.A.R. 39-1-2](https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/kansas/K-A-R-39-1-2) (Cornell LII mirror of the Kansas Administrative Regulations; authorized by K.S.A. 68-2004)

> 39-1-1. (a) Entry upon and the use of the Kansas turnpike by the following shall be prohibited: (1) Pedestrians; [...]
>
> 39-1-2. Solicitation of rides, commonly known as hitchhiking, on any portion of the turnpike is prohibited. Loitering in or about toll plazas or any other portion of the turnpike is prohibited. Stopping of vehicles by patrons for the purpose of picking up or discharging hitchhikers is prohibited.

**What it means:** The Kansas Turnpike is completely off-limits to hitchhikers: no walking, no thumbing, no waiting around toll plazas. It is also illegal for a driver to stop on the turnpike to pick you up or let you out. Get dropped off before the toll plaza, on the public road.

### K.S.A. 8-2116 and 8-2118: Classification and fines

**Source:** [K.S.A. 8-2116](https://www.ksrevisor.gov/statutes/chapters/ch08/008_021_0016.html) and [K.S.A. 8-2118](https://www.ksrevisor.gov/statutes/chapters/ch08/008_021_0018.html) (8-2118 last amended L. 2025, ch. 7, § 2)

> 8-2116. (a) Every person convicted of violating K.S.A. 8-2503, and amendments thereto, or violating any of the sections listed in the uniform fine schedule in K.S.A. 8-2118, and amendments thereto, is guilty of a traffic infraction.
>
> (b) Except where another penalty or class of misdemeanor is provided by statute, every person convicted of violating any provision of the uniform act regulating traffic on highways designated as a misdemeanor is guilty of a class C misdemeanor [...]
>
> 8-2118(c) uniform fine schedule (excerpt): "Soliciting ride or business on roadway / 8-1538 / $45" [...] "Improper use of roadway by pedestrian / 8-1537 / $45"

**What it means:** Soliciting a ride from the roadway is a traffic infraction with a $45 scheduled fine plus court costs. Disobeying a posted freeway restriction under 8-1525(b) is a class C misdemeanor, with escalating classes for repeat offenses within a year.

jurisdictions.title: Missouri (US-MO)
jurisdictions.statusLine: Legal. No Missouri statute that we could find prohibits soliciting a ride. General pedestrian rules apply, and cities may add their own ordinances. We found no statute expressly banning pedestrians from interstates.

sections.summary:
Missouri's traffic laws (Chapters 300 and 304 of the Revised Statutes of Missouri) contain no "soliciting a ride" section of the Uniform Vehicle Code type. We searched the section titles of both chapters, the Model Traffic Ordinance, and the revisor's site for "solicit" and "hitchhik" and found nothing. As far as state law goes, standing by the road with your thumb out is not specifically prohibited.

What applies to hitchhikers:

- **Walk on the sidewalk if there is one.** Otherwise walk on the left side of the roadway or its shoulder, facing traffic (§ 300.405). This rule is part of the Model Traffic Ordinance, which applies in cities that adopt it.
- **Stay off the travel lanes.** Missouri defines "roadway" as excluding the berm and shoulder, so the shoulder is the place to stand.
- **Interstates:** No statute or Missouri Highways and Transportation Commission rule banning pedestrians from interstates was found. That doesn't make interstates a good idea. Expect troopers to move you along, and city ordinances may ban it. Hitchhike from on-ramps on the surface road or from truck stops.
- **Check city ordinances.** Cities such as St. Louis and Kansas City have their own traffic codes. These were not checked here.
sections.laws:
### Mo. Rev. Stat. § 300.405: Pedestrians walking along roadways (Model Traffic Ordinance)

**Source:** [Missouri Revisor of Statutes, RSMo § 300.405](https://revisor.mo.gov/main/OneSection.aspx?section=300.405) (effective 28 Aug 1965; L. 1965 p. 445 § 88)

> 1. Where sidewalks are provided it shall be unlawful for any pedestrian to walk along and upon an adjacent roadway.
> 2. Where sidewalks are not provided any pedestrian walking along and upon a highway shall when practicable walk only on the left side of the roadway or its shoulder facing traffic which may approach from the opposite direction.

**What it means:** Use the sidewalk if there is one. Otherwise walk on the left side, on the shoulder if possible, facing oncoming traffic. Nothing here forbids standing on the shoulder asking for a ride.

### Mo. Rev. Stat. § 300.010: Definitions (Model Traffic Ordinance)

**Source:** [Missouri Revisor of Statutes, RSMo § 300.010](https://revisor.mo.gov/main/OneSection.aspx?section=300.010) (effective 28 Aug 2021)

> (7) "Controlled access highway", every highway, street or roadway in respect to which owners or occupants of abutting lands and other persons have no legal right of access to or from the same except at such points only and in such manner as may be determined by the public authority having jurisdiction over the highway, street or roadway;
>
> [...]
>
> (31) "Roadway", that portion of a highway improved, designed or ordinarily used for vehicular travel, exclusive of the berm or shoulder. In the event a highway includes two or more separate roadways the term "roadway" as used herein shall refer to any such roadway separately but not to all such roadways collectively;

**What it means:** The shoulder is not part of the roadway. In cities that use the Model Traffic Ordinance, the roadway rules apply to the travel lanes only.

### Mo. Rev. Stat. § 300.600: Cities may adopt ordinance by reference

**Source:** [Missouri Revisor of Statutes, RSMo § 300.600](https://revisor.mo.gov/main/OneSection.aspx?section=300.600) (effective 28 Aug 1965)

> This ordinance or any designated part thereof shall become effective in any city of the state upon the adoption thereof by the legislative body of the city by an ordinance appropriately describing this ordinance or the part thereof adopted. [...]

**What it means:** Chapter 300 is a model code. Its rules, including § 300.405, apply only in cities that have adopted it, and a city may have its own different rules.

### Mo. Rev. Stat. § 304.001: Definitions for chapter 304 and chapter 307

**Source:** [Missouri Revisor of Statutes, RSMo § 304.001](https://revisor.mo.gov/main/OneSection.aspx?section=304.001) (effective 28 Aug 2021; A.L. 2021 S.B. 176)

> (6) "Freeway", a divided state highway with four or more lanes, with no access to the throughways except the established interchanges and with no at-grade crossings;
> (7) "Interstate highway", a state highway included in the national system of interstate highways located within the boundaries of Missouri, [...]
> [...]
> (11) "Right-of-way", the entire width of land between the boundary lines of a state highway, including any roadway;
> (12) "Roadway", that portion of a state highway ordinarily used for vehicular travel, exclusive of the berm or shoulder;

**What it means:** On state highways, too, the "roadway" excludes the shoulder. Stand on the shoulder, not in a lane.

jurisdictions.title: Nebraska (US-NE)
jurisdictions.statusLine: Restricted. On ordinary roads you may not stand *in the roadway* to solicit a ride. The roadway excludes the berm and shoulder. On freeways, including their approach and exit ramps, "hitchhikers or walkers" are banned by name.

sections.summary:
Nebraska has two rules that matter to hitchhikers:

1. **All highways (§ 60-6,157):** "no person shall stand in a roadway for the purpose of soliciting a ride". Nebraska's "roadway" excludes the berm and shoulder, so thumbing from the shoulder or curb of an ordinary road is not banned by this section.
2. **Freeways (§ 60-6,144):** use of and entry onto a freeway is prohibited at all times for "pedestrians except in areas specifically designated for that purpose" and for "hitchhikers or walkers". The only exception is a permit from the Department of Transportation or the local authority. "Freeway" is defined to include "all interchanges and approach and exit roads thereto". That means the ramps.

What applies to hitchhikers:

- **Don't hitchhike on I-80 or any other freeway, including its on-ramps.** Stand on the surface road before the ramp begins.
- **On other roads, stay out of the travel lanes.** Shoulders and curbs are outside the "roadway" rule.
- **Penalty:** a traffic infraction. Fines are up to $100 for a first offense, $200 for a second within a year, and $300 for a third.
sections.laws:
### Neb. Rev. Stat. § 60-6,157: Pedestrians soliciting rides or business

**Source:** [Nebraska Legislature, Neb. Rev. Stat. § 60-6,157](https://nebraskalegislature.gov/laws/statutes.php?statute=60-6,157) (official; source: Laws 1973, LB 45, § 47; Laws 1993, LB 370, § 253; Laws 2009, LB278, § 1)

> (1) Except as otherwise provided in subsection (3) of this section, no person shall stand in a roadway for the purpose of soliciting a ride, employment, contributions, or business from the occupant of any vehicle.
>
> (2) No person shall stand on or in proximity to a highway for the purposes of soliciting the watching or guarding of any vehicle while parked or about to be parked on a highway.
>
> (3)(a) Any municipality may, by ordinance, allow pedestrians over the age of eighteen to enter one or more roadways, except roadways that are part of the state highway system, at specified times and locations and approach vehicles when stopped by traffic control devices or traffic control signals for the purpose of soliciting contributions which are to be devoted to charitable or community betterment purposes. [...]

**What it means:** Don't stand in a travel lane to ask for a ride. The shoulder and curb are not the "roadway" (see § 60-656 below). The subsection (3) exception covers charity collections only, not rides.

### Neb. Rev. Stat. § 60-6,144: Restrictions on use of controlled-access highway

**Source:** [Nebraska Legislature, Neb. Rev. Stat. § 60-6,144](https://nebraskalegislature.gov/laws/statutes.php?statute=60-6,144) (official; last amended Laws 2017, LB339, § 201)

> Use of a freeway and entry thereon by the following shall be prohibited at all times except by permit from the Department of Transportation or from the local authority in the case of freeways not under the jurisdiction of the department:
> (1) Pedestrians except in areas specifically designated for that purpose;
> (2) Hitchhikers or walkers;
> [...]
> (14) Any person standing on or near a roadway for the purpose of soliciting or selling to an occupant of any vehicle; [...]

**What it means:** This is a flat statutory ban. No sign is needed. You may not walk on, enter, or hitchhike on a freeway. Item (14) also covers standing "on or near" a freeway roadway to solicit, so the shoulder is no defense on a freeway.

### Neb. Rev. Stat. § 60-6,145: Official signs on controlled-access highway

**Source:** [Nebraska Legislature, Neb. Rev. Stat. § 60-6,145](https://nebraskalegislature.gov/laws/statutes.php?statute=60-6,145)

> The Department of Transportation and local authorities shall erect and maintain at appropriate locations official signs on freeways under their respective jurisdictions apprising motorists of the restrictions placed upon the use of such highways by the Nebraska Rules of the Road. [...] When such signs are erected, no person shall violate the restrictions stated on such signs.

**What it means:** Signs at freeway entrances restate the ban. The ban in § 60-6,144 applies whether or not a sign is posted.

### Neb. Rev. Stat. §§ 60-621, 60-656, 60-661, 60-624: Definitions

**Source:** [§ 60-621](https://nebraskalegislature.gov/laws/statutes.php?statute=60-621), [§ 60-656](https://nebraskalegislature.gov/laws/statutes.php?statute=60-656), [§ 60-661](https://nebraskalegislature.gov/laws/statutes.php?statute=60-661), [§ 60-624](https://nebraskalegislature.gov/laws/statutes.php?statute=60-624)

> 60-621. Freeway shall mean a divided arterial highway designed primarily for through traffic with full control of access and with grade separations at all intersecting road crossings, including all interchanges and approach and exit roads thereto.
>
> 60-656. Roadway shall mean that portion of a highway improved, designed, or ordinarily used for vehicular travel, exclusive of the berm or shoulder. If a highway includes two or more separate roadways, the term roadway shall refer to any such roadway separately but not to all such roadways collectively.
>
> 60-661. Shoulder shall mean that part of the highway contiguous to the roadway and designed for the accommodation of stopped vehicles, for emergency use, and for lateral support of the base and surface courses of the roadway.
>
> 60-624. Highway shall mean the entire width between the boundary limits of any street, road, avenue, boulevard, or way which is publicly maintained when any part thereof is open to the use of the public for purposes of vehicular travel.

**What it means:** Freeway ramps ("approach and exit roads") are part of the freeway, so the hitchhiker ban starts where the ramp starts. On non-freeway roads, the shoulder is outside the "roadway" and outside § 60-6,157.

### Neb. Rev. Stat. § 60-6,156: Pedestrians on highways and roadways

**Source:** [Nebraska Legislature, Neb. Rev. Stat. § 60-6,156](https://nebraskalegislature.gov/laws/statutes.php?statute=60-6,156)

> (1) Where a sidewalk is provided and its use is practicable, it shall be unlawful for any pedestrian to walk along and upon an adjacent roadway or shoulder.
>
> (2) Where a sidewalk is not available and a shoulder is available, any pedestrian walking along and upon a highway shall walk only on the shoulder as far as practicable from the edge of the roadway.
>
> (3) Where neither a sidewalk nor a shoulder is available, any pedestrian who walks along and upon a highway shall walk as near as practicable to the edge of the roadway and, if on a two-way roadway, shall walk only on the left side of such roadway.

**What it means:** Where there's a sidewalk, you may not walk on the shoulder either. Use the sidewalk.

### Neb. Rev. Stat. §§ 60-682 and 60-689: Penalty

**Source:** [§ 60-682](https://nebraskalegislature.gov/laws/statutes.php?statute=60-682) and [§ 60-689](https://nebraskalegislature.gov/laws/statutes.php?statute=60-689)

> 60-682. Unless otherwise declared in the Nebraska Rules of the Road with respect to particular offenses, a violation of any provision of the rules shall constitute a traffic infraction.
>
> 60-689. Any person who is found guilty of a traffic infraction in violation of the Nebraska Rules of the Road for which a penalty has not been specifically provided shall be fined: (1) Not more than one hundred dollars for the first offense; (2) Not more than two hundred dollars for a second offense within a one-year period; and (3) Not more than three hundred dollars for a third and subsequent offense within a one-year period.

**What it means:** Hitchhiking on a freeway or soliciting from the roadway is a traffic infraction. It is fine-only: up to $100, then $200, then $300 for repeats within a year.

jurisdictions.title: North Dakota (US-ND)
jurisdictions.statusLine: Restricted. You may not stand *in a roadway* to solicit a ride. The roadway excludes the berm and shoulder, so thumbing from the shoulder or curb is not covered by this rule. No statute bans pedestrians from interstates. The state can ban them on a controlled-access roadway by order plus posted signs, but no such order was found.

sections.summary:
North Dakota has the Uniform Vehicle Code rule: "No person may stand in a roadway for the purpose of soliciting a ride" (N.D.C.C. § 39-10-34(1)). "Roadway" is defined as "exclusive of the berm or shoulder". Hitchhiking from the shoulder or curb is not prohibited by this section.

What applies to hitchhikers:

- **Stay out of the travel lanes.** A violation is a noncriminal traffic violation. The statutory fee is $20 for most moving violations.
- **Interstates (I-94, I-29):** the director of the Department of Transportation (by order) or local authorities (by ordinance) may ban classes of traffic from controlled-access roadways. Any ban is enforceable where official traffic-control devices (signs) are posted. No statute bans pedestrians on interstates outright. A December 2025 news report quoted the Highway Patrol: "In North Dakota we do not have a law saying you can't walk or bike along the interstate system." Even so, stay far from the lanes, and obey any posted sign.
- **Walk on the sidewalk** if there is one, otherwise on the shoulder. With neither, walk on the left edge facing traffic.
sections.laws:
### N.D.C.C. § 39-10-34: Pedestrian soliciting ride or business

**Source:** [North Dakota Legislative Branch, N.D.C.C. ch. 39-10 (PDF)](https://www.ndlegis.gov/cencode/t39c10.pdf) (official; PDF generated July 1, 2025)

> 1. No person may stand in a roadway for the purpose of soliciting a ride.
> 2. No person may stand in a roadway for the purpose of soliciting employment, business, or contributions from the occupant of any vehicle.
> 3. No person may stand on or in proximity to a street or highway for the purpose of soliciting the watching or guarding of any vehicle while parked or about to be parked on a street or highway.

**What it means:** Don't stand in a travel lane to ask for a ride. The shoulder is not part of the roadway, so standing on it with your thumb out is not covered by this section.

### N.D.C.C. § 39-01-01: Definitions

**Source:** [North Dakota Legislative Branch, N.D.C.C. ch. 39-01 (PDF)](https://www.ndlegis.gov/cencode/t39c01.pdf)

> 12. "Controlled-access highway" means every highway, street, or roadway in respect to which owners or occupants of abutting lands and other persons have no legal right of access to or from the same except at such points only and in such manner as may be determined by the public authority having jurisdiction over such highway, street, or roadway.
> [...]
> 76. "Roadway" means that portion of a highway improved, designed, or ordinarily used for vehicular travel, exclusive of the berm or shoulder. In the event a highway includes two or more separate roadways, the term "roadway" as used herein refers to any such roadway separately but not to all such roadways collectively.

**What it means:** The ride-solicitation ban stops at the edge of the travel lanes.

### N.D.C.C. § 39-10-33: Pedestrian on roadway

**Source:** [North Dakota Legislative Branch, N.D.C.C. ch. 39-10 (PDF)](https://www.ndlegis.gov/cencode/t39c10.pdf)

> 1. Where a sidewalk is provided and its use is practicable, it is unlawful for any pedestrian to walk along and upon an adjacent roadway.
> 2. Where a sidewalk is not available, any pedestrian walking along and upon a highway shall walk only on a shoulder, as far as practicable from the edge of the roadway.
> 3. Where neither a sidewalk nor a shoulder is available, any pedestrian walking along and upon a highway shall walk as near as practicable to an outside edge of the roadway, and, if on a two-way roadway, shall walk only on the left side of the roadway.
> 4. Except as otherwise provided for in this chapter, any pedestrian upon a roadway shall yield the right of way to all vehicles upon the roadway.

**What it means:** Sidewalk first, then the shoulder, then the left edge facing traffic.

### N.D.C.C. § 39-10-21: Restrictions on use of controlled-access roadway

**Source:** [North Dakota Legislative Branch, N.D.C.C. ch. 39-10 (PDF)](https://www.ndlegis.gov/cencode/t39c10.pdf)

> The director may by order, and local authorities may by ordinance, with respect to any controlled-access roadway under their respective jurisdictions, prohibit the use of any such roadway by any class or kind of traffic which is found incompatible with the normal and safe movement of traffic.
>
> The director or the local authority adopting any such prohibition shall erect and maintain official traffic-control devices on the controlled-access roadway on which such prohibitions are applicable and when in place no person may disobey the restrictions stated on such devices.

**What it means:** Pedestrian bans on interstates depend on an order plus posted signs. If a ramp is signed against pedestrians, stay before the sign.

### N.D.C.C. §§ 39-06.1-02, 39-06.1-06, 39-06.1-09: Noncriminal disposition and fees

**Source:** [North Dakota Legislative Branch, N.D.C.C. ch. 39-06.1 (PDF)](https://www.ndlegis.gov/cencode/t39c06-1.pdf)

> 39-06.1-02. 1. An individual cited, in accordance with sections 39-07-07 and 39-07-08, for a traffic violation under state law or municipal ordinance, other than an offense listed in section 39-06.1-05, is deemed to be charged with a noncriminal offense. [...]
>
> 39-06.1-06. [...] 2. For a moving violation as defined in section 39-06.1-09, a fee of twenty dollars, except for: [...]
>
> 39-06.1-09. For the purposes of sections 39-06.1-06 and 39-06.1-13, a "moving violation" means [...] a violation of the provisions of chapter 39-10, 39-10.2, 39-21, or 39-27, or equivalent ordinances, except [...]

**What it means:** Section 39-10-34 is in chapter 39-10 and is not listed among the exceptions. A citation for soliciting a ride from the roadway is therefore a noncriminal moving violation with a $20 statutory fee. Moving violations can also put points on a driver's license record under § 39-06.1-10.

jurisdictions.title: Oklahoma (US-OK)
jurisdictions.statusLine: Restricted. You may not stand *in a roadway* to solicit a ride, and hitchhiking anywhere on a turnpike is banned outright. Off the turnpikes, the roadway excludes the shoulder, so thumbing from the shoulder or curb of an ordinary road is not covered by the roadway rule.

sections.summary:
Oklahoma has two hitchhiking rules:

1. **Ordinary roads (47 O.S. § 11-507):** "No person shall stand in a roadway for the purpose of soliciting a ride, donation, employment or business from the occupant of any vehicle". Oklahoma's definition of "roadway" excludes the shoulder.
2. **Turnpikes (47 O.S. § 11-1401(E)):** "It shall be unlawful for any person to travel a turnpike on foot except to leave or service a disabled vehicle, or for any person to hitchhike on a turnpike." You also may not enter the fenced part of a turnpike except in a vehicle at an authorized entrance.

What applies to hitchhikers:

- **Never hitchhike on a turnpike** (any Oklahoma Turnpike Authority toll road). Get dropped off on a public road before the toll road begins.
- **On other roads, stay out of the travel lanes.** The shoulder is not part of the roadway.
- **Free (non-toll) interstates and freeways:** ODOT or local authorities can ban pedestrians from controlled-access roadways by posting signs. Obey any posted sign.
- **Penalty:** a misdemeanor, fine of $5 to $500 or up to 10 days in jail for a first offense.
sections.laws:
### 47 O.S. § 11-507: Pedestrians soliciting rides or business

**Source:** [Oklahoma Legislature, Oklahoma Statutes Title 47 (complete title PDF)](https://www.oklegislature.gov/OK_Statutes/CompleteTitles/os47.pdf) (official compilation dated December 31, 2025)

> No person shall stand in a roadway for the purpose of soliciting a ride, donation, employment or business from the occupant of any vehicle; provided, that persons shall not be prohibited from soliciting pursuant to this section if performed on a roadway maintained by a city or town in compliance with a permit and regulations adopted by ordinance.
>
> Added by Laws 1961, p. 380, § 11-507. Amended by Laws 2021, c. 158, § 1, emerg. eff. April 22, 2021.

**What it means:** Don't stand in a travel lane to ask for a ride. On an ordinary road the shoulder is not the roadway (see § 1-158 below), so the shoulder or curb is outside this rule. The 2021 amendment lets cities issue permits for roadway solicitation. In practice that is meant for charity collections, not hitchhikers.

### 47 O.S. § 11-1401: Turnpikes, unlawful acts

**Source:** [Oklahoma Legislature, Oklahoma Statutes Title 47 (complete title PDF)](https://www.oklegislature.gov/OK_Statutes/CompleteTitles/os47.pdf)

> A. It shall be unlawful for any person to enter that part of a turnpike enclosed by fence except in a vehicle at authorized entrances.
> [...]
> D. It shall be unlawful for any person to cross a turnpike except at grade separations provided for cross traffic or through drainage structures under the turnpike.
>
> E. It shall be unlawful for any person to travel a turnpike on foot except to leave or service a disabled vehicle, or for any person to hitchhike on a turnpike.
> [...]
> M. Any person who violates any provision of this section shall, upon conviction, be guilty of a misdemeanor and shall be punished as provided in Section 17-101 of this title.
>
> [...] Laws 2021, c. 243, § 1, eff. Nov. 1, 2021.

**What it means:** This is Oklahoma's strictest rule. Hitchhiking on a turnpike is banned anywhere on it, shoulder included. You may not walk onto the fenced turnpike right-of-way at all. Hitchhike on the public road before the turnpike entrance.

### 47 O.S. § 1-158: Roadway and shoulder (definitions)

**Source:** [Oklahoma Legislature, Oklahoma Statutes Title 47 (complete title PDF)](https://www.oklegislature.gov/OK_Statutes/CompleteTitles/os47.pdf)

> (a) Roadway. That portion of a highway improved, designed or ordinarily used for vehicular travel, exclusive of the shoulder. In the event a highway includes two or more separate roadways the term "roadway" as used herein shall refer to any such roadway separately but not to all such roadways collectively.
>
> (b) Shoulder. The portion of the roadway contiguous with the traveled way for accommodation of stopped vehicles, for emergency use, and for lateral support of base and surface courses.

**What it means:** Subsection (a) says the roadway is "exclusive of the shoulder", which supports hitchhiking from the shoulder. Oddly, subsection (b) calls the shoulder "the portion of the roadway contiguous with the traveled way". A police officer could read that wording against you. The safest spot is clearly off the pavement or behind a curb.

### 47 O.S. § 11-313: Restrictions on use of controlled-access roadway

**Source:** [Oklahoma Legislature, Oklahoma Statutes Title 47 (complete title PDF)](https://www.oklegislature.gov/OK_Statutes/CompleteTitles/os47.pdf)

> The Department of Transportation, the Oklahoma Transportation Authority, or local authorities may, with respect to any controlled-access roadway under their respective jurisdictions, prohibit the use of any such roadway by pedestrians, bicycles or other non-motorized traffic or by any person operating a motor-driven cycle. The Department of Transportation, the Oklahoma Transportation Authority, or local authorities adopting any such prohibitory regulations shall erect and maintain official signs on the controlled-access roadway on which such regulations are applicable and when so erected no person shall disobey the restrictions stated on such signs.

**What it means:** On free (non-toll) interstates and freeways, a pedestrian ban applies where it is signed. Stand at the ramp entrance, before any "pedestrians prohibited" sign.

### 47 O.S. § 11-506: Pedestrians on roadways or bridges

**Source:** [Oklahoma Legislature, Oklahoma Statutes Title 47 (complete title PDF)](https://www.oklegislature.gov/OK_Statutes/CompleteTitles/os47.pdf)

> (a) Where sidewalks are provided, it shall be unlawful for any pedestrian to walk along and upon an adjacent roadway.
>
> (b) Where sidewalks are not provided, any pedestrian walking along and upon a highway shall, when practicable, walk only on the left side of the roadway or its shoulder facing traffic which may approach from the opposite direction and shall yield to approaching vehicles.
>
> (c) [...] it shall be unlawful for a pedestrian to use a bridge where sidewalks are not provided for the purpose of standing or sightseeing.

**What it means:** Walk facing traffic. Don't stand on a bridge without a sidewalk to hitchhike.

### 47 O.S. § 17-101: Misdemeanor violations, penalties

**Source:** [Oklahoma Legislature, Oklahoma Statutes Title 47 (complete title PDF)](https://www.oklegislature.gov/OK_Statutes/CompleteTitles/os47.pdf)

> A. It is a misdemeanor for any person to violate any of the provisions of this title unless such violation is by this title or other law of this state declared to be a felony.
>
> B. 1. Every person convicted of a misdemeanor for a violation of any of the provisions of Sections 10-101 through 14-121 or Sections 16-101 through 16-114 of this title for which another penalty is not provided shall upon conviction thereof be punished by a fine of not less than Five Dollars ($5.00) nor more than Five Hundred Dollars ($500.00) or by imprisonment for not more than ten (10) days; for a second such conviction within one (1) year after the first conviction by imprisonment for not more than twenty (20) days; upon a third or subsequent conviction within one (1) year after the first conviction by imprisonment for not more than six (6) months, or by both such fine and imprisonment.

**What it means:** Sections 11-507, 11-1401 and 11-313 all fall within §§ 10-101 through 14-121. A first offense means a fine of $5 to $500 or up to 10 days in jail. Repeat offenses within a year can mean longer jail terms.

jurisdictions.title: South Dakota (US-SD)
jurisdictions.statusLine: Legal. No South Dakota statute prohibits soliciting a ride. Pedestrians can be banned from controlled-access highways only by a Transportation Commission rule (or a local ordinance) plus posted signs.

sections.summary:
South Dakota is one of the few states without the Uniform Vehicle Code "no person shall stand in a roadway for the purpose of soliciting a ride" section. Chapter 32-27 (Pedestrians' Rights and Duties) has no soliciting provision. A search of Title 32 (Motor Vehicles) and the highway chapters found no hitchhiking statute.

What still applies to hitchhikers:

- **Walk facing traffic** on the left side of the road or its shoulder where there is no sidewalk (a petty offense if you don't).
- **Interstates (I-90, I-29, I-190, I-229):** the Transportation Commission may ban pedestrians from a controlled-access roadway by formal rule, and local authorities may do so by ordinance. Once signs are erected, disobeying them is a Class 2 misdemeanor. I found no such Transportation Commission rule in the traffic-safety chapter of the Administrative Rules (ARSD 70:01:03). Obey any sign you see at a ramp.
- **Don't block traffic.** Obstructing vehicular or pedestrian traffic can be charged as disorderly conduct (SDCL 22-18-35).
- **Cities can have their own rules.** For example, Sioux Falls reportedly bans standing in a roadway to solicit a ride (not verified here).
sections.laws:
### SDCL § 32-27-5: Highways without sidewalks, duty to walk facing traffic

**Source:** [South Dakota Legislature, SDCL 32-27-5](https://sdlegislature.gov/Statutes/32-27-5) (official; source: SL 1961, ch 151; SL 1989, ch 255, § 187)

> Where sidewalks are not provided any pedestrian walking along or upon a highway shall, when practicable, walk only on the left side of the roadway or its shoulder facing traffic which may approach from the opposite direction. A violation of this section is a petty offense.

**What it means:** Walk against traffic. Standing still on the shoulder with your thumb out is not addressed by any statute.

### SDCL § 32-26-11: Prohibition of pedestrians on controlled-access highway

**Source:** [South Dakota Legislature, SDCL 32-26-11](https://sdlegislature.gov/Statutes/32-26-11) (official; source: SL 1961, ch 150, § 3; SL 1987, ch 210, § 35; SL 1989, ch 255, §§ 163, 182)

> The transportation commission may, by rule adopted pursuant to chapter 1-26, and local authorities may by ordinance, with respect to any controlled-access roadway under their respective jurisdictions, prohibit the use of any such roadway by pedestrians, bicycles, or other nonmotorized traffic or by any person operating a motor-driven cycle. The Department of Transportation or the local authority adopting any such prohibitory regulation shall erect and maintain official signs on the controlled-access roadway on which such regulations are applicable. If so erected no person may disobey the restrictions stated on such signs. The violation for failure to obey a regulatory sign under this section is a Class 2 misdemeanor.

**What it means:** No statute bans pedestrians on interstates outright. A ban requires a formal rule (or a city or county ordinance) and signs. Where a sign prohibits pedestrians, disobeying it is a Class 2 misdemeanor: up to 30 days in jail and/or a $500 fine (SDCL 22-6-2). The safest place to hitchhike is at the start of the on-ramp.

### SDCL § 32-14-1: Definitions

**Source:** [South Dakota Legislature, SDCL 32-14-1](https://sdlegislature.gov/Statutes/32-14-1)

> (11) "Highway," the entire width between the boundary lines of every way publicly maintained when any part thereof is open to the use of the public as a matter of right for purposes of vehicular travel;
> [...]
> (27) "Roadway," that portion of a highway improved, designed, or ordinarily used for vehicular travel, exclusive of the berm or shoulder. If a highway includes two or more separate roadways, the term, roadway, refers to any such roadway separately but not to all such roadways collectively;

**What it means:** The shoulder is not part of the roadway. This matters for any local ordinance written in "roadway" terms.

### SDCL § 22-18-35: Disorderly conduct

**Source:** [South Dakota Legislature, SDCL 22-18-35](https://sdlegislature.gov/Statutes/22-18-35)

> Any person who intentionally causes serious public inconvenience, annoyance, or alarm to any other person, or creates a risk thereof by: [...] (4) Obstructing vehicular or pedestrian traffic; is guilty of disorderly conduct. Disorderly conduct is a Class 2 misdemeanor. [...]

**What it means:** Hitchhiking itself is legal. Deliberately getting in the way of traffic, for example by stepping into the lane to make cars stop, can be charged as disorderly conduct.

### SDCL § 22-6-2: Misdemeanor classes and penalties

**Source:** [South Dakota Legislature, SDCL 22-6-2](https://sdlegislature.gov/Statutes/22-6-2)

> (2) Class 2 misdemeanor: thirty days imprisonment in a county jail or five hundred dollars fine, or both.

**What it means:** This is the maximum penalty for ignoring a posted freeway pedestrian ban under § 32-26-11.

jurisdictions.title: Arizona (US-AZ)
jurisdictions.statusLine: Restricted. You may not stand *in a roadway* to solicit a ride from a driver. The roadway excludes the berm and shoulder, so the statute does not reach hitchhiking from the shoulder. Pedestrians can be banned from controlled-access highways where signs are posted.

sections.summary:
Arizona has the classic Uniform Vehicle Code hitchhiking rule in A.R.S. § 28-796(C): "A person shall not stand in a roadway for the purpose of soliciting a ride from the driver of a vehicle." Arizona's definition of "roadway" is "exclusive of the berm or shoulder". Standing on the shoulder, curb or sidewalk to hitchhike is not covered by this rule.

What applies to hitchhikers:

- **Stay out of the travel lanes.** A violation is a civil traffic violation (a fine, not a crime). The maximum civil penalty is generally $250 plus surcharges.
- **Freeways:** ADOT's director or a city or county may ban pedestrians from a controlled-access highway. Once the signs are up, you must obey them. Stand at the ramp entrance before any "pedestrians prohibited" sign.
- **Walk on the sidewalk** where there is one. Otherwise walk on the left side of the road or its shoulder, facing traffic.
- **Proposed median and ramp bans were not enacted.** Bills in 2024 and 2025 would have banned pedestrians from congregating or soliciting on medians and freeway ramps (see History).
sections.laws:
### A.R.S. § 28-796: Pedestrian on roadways

**Source:** [Arizona Legislature, A.R.S. § 28-796](https://www.azleg.gov/ars/28/00796.htm) (official site, current text)

> A. If sidewalks are provided, a pedestrian shall not walk along and on an adjacent roadway.
>
> B. If sidewalks are not provided, a pedestrian walking along and on a highway shall walk when practicable only on the left side of the roadway or its shoulder facing traffic that may approach from the opposite direction.
>
> C. A person shall not stand in a roadway for the purpose of soliciting a ride from the driver of a vehicle.

**What it means:** Subsection C is the hitchhiking rule. It applies only to the "roadway", meaning the travel lanes. Standing on the shoulder or behind the curb is not banned by this section. Pick a spot with room for a car to pull fully off the road.

### A.R.S. § 28-601: Definitions (chapter 3, traffic and vehicle regulation)

**Source:** [Arizona Legislature, A.R.S. § 28-601](https://www.azleg.gov/ars/28/00601.htm)

> 2. "Controlled access highway" means a highway, street or roadway to or from which owners or occupants of abutting lands and other persons have no legal right of access except at such points only and in the manner determined by the public authority that has jurisdiction over the highway, street or roadway.
> [...]
> 22. "Roadway" means that portion of a highway that is improved, designed or ordinarily used for vehicular travel, exclusive of the berm or shoulder. If a highway includes two or more separate roadways, roadway refers to any such roadway separately but not to all such roadways collectively.

**What it means:** The shoulder is not part of the roadway. The § 28-796(C) ban therefore stops at the white edge line.

### A.R.S. § 28-733: Restrictions on use of controlled access highway

**Source:** [Arizona Legislature, A.R.S. § 28-733](https://www.azleg.gov/ars/28/00733.htm)

> A. The director may, and local authorities by ordinance may, prohibit the use of any part of a controlled access highway under their respective jurisdictions by pedestrians, bicycles or other nonmotorized traffic or by any person operating a motor driven cycle.
>
> B. The director or the local authority adopting the prohibition prescribed in subsection A shall erect and maintain official signs on the applicable controlled access highway. When the signs are erected, a person shall not disobey the restrictions stated on the signs.

**What it means:** Pedestrian bans on Arizona freeways depend on signs. Where a sign prohibits pedestrians, walking or standing past it is a violation. Hitchhike from the surface street before the ramp, or from a gas station or truck stop.

### A.R.S. §§ 28-121 and 28-1598: Penalty

**Source:** [Arizona Legislature, A.R.S. § 28-121](https://www.azleg.gov/ars/28/00121.htm) and [A.R.S. § 28-1598](https://www.azleg.gov/ars/28/01598.htm)

> 28-121. B. A violation of or failure or refusal to do or perform an act or thing required by chapter 3, 5, 7 or 8 or chapter 9, article 4 of this title is a civil traffic violation unless the statute defining the violation provides for a different classification. [...]
>
> 28-1598. Except as otherwise provided, a civil penalty imposed pursuant to this article shall not exceed two hundred fifty dollars. In addition, the court shall levy surcharges pursuant to sections 12-116.01 and 12-116.02.

**What it means:** Sections 28-796 and 28-733 are in chapter 3 of Title 28, so a violation is a civil traffic violation. That means a fine of up to $250 plus state surcharges, not a criminal charge.

### A.R.S. § 13-2906: Obstructing a highway or other public thoroughfare

**Source:** [Arizona Legislature, A.R.S. § 13-2906](https://www.azleg.gov/ars/13/02906.htm)

> A. A person commits obstructing a highway or other public thoroughfare if the person, alone or with other persons, does any of the following:
> 1. Having no legal privilege to do so, recklessly interferes with the passage of any highway or public thoroughfare by creating an unreasonable inconvenience or hazard.
> 2. Intentionally activates a pedestrian signal on a highway or public thoroughfare if the person's reason for activating the signal is not to cross the highway or public thoroughfare but to do both of the following:
> (a) Stop the passage of traffic on the highway or public thoroughfare.
> (b) Solicit a driver for a donation or business.
> [...]
> B. Obstructing a highway or other public thoroughfare under: [...]
> 2. Subsection A, paragraph 1 of this section is a class 2 misdemeanor, except that a second or subsequent violation within a period of twenty-four months is a class 1 misdemeanor.
> 3. Subsection A, paragraph 2 of this section is a class 3 misdemeanor.

**What it means:** This is a criminal law, separate from the traffic code. Hitchhiking in a way that creates an unreasonable hazard or blocks traffic can be charged as a class 2 misdemeanor. Paragraph 2 names donations and business, not rides. Don't push the walk button to stop cars so you can ask them for a lift.
sections.history:
### Vetoed and pending median and ramp bills (2024 to 2025)

**Source:** [2025 H.B. 2684 (introduced), "pedestrians; congregating; medians; unsafe locations"](https://www.azleg.gov/legtext/57leg/1r/bills/hb2684p.htm)

H.B. 2684 would have added a new § 28-798: "A pedestrian may not congregate or engage in solicitation if the pedestrian is any of the following: 1. on a painted or raised traffic island or median. 2. on an exit or entrance ramp or roadway of a controlled access highway. 3. in an unsafe location where there is not a sidewalk or a safe corridor for pedestrians." Its penalties were a warning for a first offense, a civil traffic violation for a second, and a class 1 misdemeanor after that. As of 2026-11-02, A.R.S. § 28-798 does not exist on the Legislature's site (the URL returns "page not found"), so the bill is not codified law. A similar 2024 bill, H.B. 2658, passed both chambers and was vetoed, according to the Legislature's House bill summary marked "Vetoed".

**What it means:** Arizona has not banned standing on freeway on-ramps as such. Check for new law before relying on this, because the idea keeps coming back.

jurisdictions.title: Nevada (US-NV)
jurisdictions.statusLine: Illegal. Nevada law says a person "shall not stand in a highway to solicit a ride". Nevada defines "highway" as the entire width between the boundary lines of the way, which includes the shoulder. Violation is a misdemeanor, though a prosecutor may choose to treat it as a civil infraction.

sections.summary:
Most states that follow the Uniform Vehicle Code ban standing in the *roadway* (the travel lanes) to hitch. Nevada's NRS 484B.297(3) uses the word *highway* instead. Nevada defines a highway as "the entire width between the boundary lines" of a public way. On its face, that covers the shoulder and everything else inside the right-of-way, so there is no safe-harbor shoulder in Nevada.

What applies to hitchhikers:

- **Don't stand anywhere on a highway, shoulder included, to solicit a ride.** Hitch from places outside the highway right-of-way, such as gas stations, truck stops and parking lots. Ask drivers directly where the property owner allows it.
- **Walking:** use the sidewalk where one exists. Otherwise walk on the left side facing traffic.
- **Controlled-access highways (freeways):** the Nevada Department of Transportation (NDOT) or a local authority may require a permit for pedestrians, or prohibit them where pedestrian use wouldn't be safe. Violating such a restriction is a civil infraction.
- **Penalty:** hitchhiking under NRS 484B.297 is a misdemeanor. Since 2021, a prosecutor may elect to treat a traffic misdemeanor as a civil infraction instead.
sections.laws:
### NRS 484B.297: Walking along highways; solicitation of ride

**Source:** [Nevada Legislature, NRS 484B.297](https://www.leg.state.nv.us/NRS/NRS-484B.html#NRS484BSec297) (history: Added 1969; amended 1991, 2001, 2015, 2019)

> 1. Except as otherwise provided in subsection 6, where sidewalks are provided, it is unlawful for any pedestrian to walk along and upon an adjacent highway.
>
> 2. Except as otherwise provided in subsection 6, pedestrians walking along highways where sidewalks are not provided shall walk on the left side of those highways facing the approaching traffic.
>
> 3. A person shall not stand in a highway to solicit a ride or any business from the driver or any occupant of a vehicle. A person shall not, without a permit issued pursuant to NRS 244.3555 or 268.423, solicit any contribution from the driver or any occupant of a vehicle.
>
> 4. It is unlawful for any pedestrian who is under the influence of intoxicating liquors or any narcotic or stupefying drug to be within the traveled portion of any highway.
> [...]
>
> 7. A person who violates the provisions of this section is guilty of a misdemeanor.

**What it means:** The ban is on standing "in a highway", not just in the travel lanes. Read with the definition below, that includes the shoulder. Find a spot off the highway itself, like a fuel station forecourt or a pull-out on private property where you have permission.

### NRS 484A.095 and 484A.220: "Highway" and "Roadway" defined

**Source:** [Nevada Legislature, NRS chapter 484A](https://www.leg.state.nv.us/NRS/NRS-484A.html#NRS484ASec095) (484A.095: Added 1969, amended 1981; 484A.220: Added 1973)

> NRS 484A.095 "Highway" means the entire width between the boundary lines of every way dedicated to a public authority when any part of the way is open to the use of the public for purposes of vehicular traffic, whether or not the public authority is maintaining the way.

> NRS 484A.220 "Roadway" means that portion of a highway which is improved and ordinarily used for vehicular traffic, exclusive of the shoulder.

**What it means:** Nevada's statutes use both terms, and the hitchhiking rule uses the broader one. The roadway excludes the shoulder. The highway includes it.

### NRS 484B.593: Restrictions on use of controlled-access highway

**Source:** [Nevada Legislature, NRS 484B.593](https://www.leg.state.nv.us/NRS/NRS-484B.html#NRS484BSec593) (history: Added 1969; amended 1979, 1987, 1991, 2009, 2021)

> 1. The Department of Transportation or a local authority, after considering the advice of the Nevada Bicycle and Pedestrian Advisory Board, may with respect to any controlled-access highway under its jurisdiction:
> (a) Require a permit for the use of the highway by pedestrians, bicycles or other nonmotorized traffic or by any person operating a power cycle; or
> (b) If it determines that the use of the highway for such a purpose would not be safe, prohibit the use of the highway by pedestrians, bicycles or other nonmotorized traffic.
>
> 2. Any person who violates any prohibition or restriction enacted pursuant to subsection 1 is guilty of a civil infraction punishable pursuant to NRS 484A.703 to 484A.705, inclusive.

**What it means:** No statute bans pedestrians from every freeway, but NDOT or a local authority may close specific freeways to them. Even where walking is allowed, standing on any part of the freeway to hitch still violates NRS 484B.297(3).

### NRS 484A.060: "Controlled-access highway" defined

**Source:** [Nevada Legislature, NRS 484A.060](https://www.leg.state.nv.us/NRS/NRS-484A.html#NRS484ASec060) (Added 1969)

> "Controlled-access highway" means every highway to or from which owners or occupants of abutting lands and other persons have no legal right of access except at such points only and in such manner as may be determined by a public authority.

**What it means:** Interstates and other freeways.

### NRS 484A.7049: Misdemeanor may be treated as civil infraction

**Source:** [Nevada Legislature, NRS 484A.7049](https://www.leg.state.nv.us/NRS/NRS-484A.html#NRS484ASec7049) (Added 2021; amended 2025)

> A prosecuting attorney may elect to treat a violation of a provision of chapters 483 to 484E, inclusive, 486 or 490 of NRS that is punishable as a misdemeanor, other than a violation of NRS 484C.110 or 484C.120, as a civil infraction pursuant to NRS 484A.703 to 484A.705, inclusive.

**What it means:** Since 2021, the default penalty for a traffic offense with no stated penalty has been a civil infraction (NRS 484A.900). The hitchhiking section still says "misdemeanor", but a prosecutor can choose to downgrade it to a civil infraction, which is not a criminal offense.

jurisdictions.title: New Mexico (US-NM)
jurisdictions.statusLine: Restricted. You may not stand *in a roadway* to solicit a ride. The roadway excludes the berm and shoulder, so thumbing from the shoulder or curb is not covered by this rule. Pedestrians can be banned from controlled-access highways where signs are posted.

sections.summary:
New Mexico uses the Uniform Vehicle Code wording: "No person shall stand in a roadway for the purpose of soliciting a ride, employment or business from the occupant of any vehicle" (NMSA § 66-7-340). New Mexico defines "roadway" as excluding "the berm or shoulder". Hitchhiking from the shoulder, curb or sidewalk is therefore not banned by state statute.

What applies to hitchhikers:

- **Stay out of the travel lanes.** Soliciting from the roadway is a "penalty assessment misdemeanor". The scheduled penalty is $25 (see § 66-8-116 below).
- **Freeways:** the State Transportation Commission or a local authority may restrict or ban classes of traffic, such as pedestrians, from a controlled-access roadway. The ban applies once signs or other official traffic-control devices are in place.
- **Walk on the sidewalk** where there is one. Otherwise walk on the left side of the road or its shoulder, facing traffic.
- **Albuquerque and Santa Fe** have median-safety ordinances that limit standing on narrow medians, according to news reports. The texts were not reviewed here. Check them if you are hitchhiking in those cities.
sections.laws:
### NMSA 1978, § 66-7-340: Pedestrians soliciting rides or business

**Source:** [FindLaw, N.M. Stat. § 66-7-340](https://codes.findlaw.com/nm/chapter-66-motor-vehicles/nm-st-sect-66-7-340/) (unofficial mirror, "current as of January 01, 2024"). The official compilation at nmonesource.com refused automated access during this session.

> A. No person shall stand in a roadway for the purpose of soliciting a ride, employment or business from the occupant of any vehicle.
>
> B. No person shall stand on or in proximity to a street or highway for the purpose of soliciting the watching or guarding of any vehicle while parked or about to be parked on a street or highway.

**What it means:** Don't step into the lanes to ask for a ride. The rule covers only the roadway, which by definition excludes the shoulder. Standing on the shoulder or behind the curb with your thumb out is not prohibited by this section.

### NMSA 1978, § 66-1-4.15: Definitions ("roadway")

**Source:** [New Mexico Legislature, 2024 S.B. 88 (as passed), § 4 amending § 66-1-4.15](https://www.nmlegis.gov/Sessions/24%20Regular/final/SB0088.PDF) (signed by the governor, Laws 2024, ch. 13). The bill restates the full section.

> Q. "roadway" means that portion of a street or highway improved, designed or ordinarily used for vehicular travel, exclusive of the berm or shoulder; when a highway includes two or more separate roadways, the term "roadway" refers to each roadway separately but not to all of the roadways collectively.

**What it means:** The shoulder is not part of the roadway. The ride-solicitation ban in § 66-7-340 applies to the travel lanes, not the shoulder.

### NMSA 1978, § 66-7-339: Pedestrians on roadways

**Source:** [New Mexico Legislature, 2024 (1st Special Session) S.B. 11 (introduced), § 5](https://www.nmlegis.gov/Sessions/24%20Special/bills/senate/SB0011.HTML). The bill reprints the existing section with proposed additions underlined. The quote below is the existing text only. The bill died, so this text remains in force. It matches the FindLaw mirror (current as of January 01, 2024).

> A. Where sidewalks are provided, it is unlawful for a pedestrian to walk along and upon an adjacent roadway.
>
> B. Where sidewalks are not provided, a pedestrian walking along and upon a highway shall, when practicable, walk only on the left side of the roadway or its shoulder facing traffic that may approach from the opposite direction.
>
> C. A person who violates the provisions of this section is guilty of a penalty assessment misdemeanor.

**What it means:** Use the sidewalk where there is one. Otherwise walk facing traffic on the left side of the road or shoulder.

### NMSA 1978, § 66-7-321: Restrictions on use of controlled-access roadway

**Source:** [FindLaw, N.M. Stat. § 66-7-321](https://codes.findlaw.com/nm/chapter-66-motor-vehicles/nm-st-sect-66-7-321/) (unofficial mirror, "current as of January 01, 2024")

> A. The state transportation commission, by resolution or order entered in its minutes, and local authorities, by ordinance, may regulate or prohibit the use of any controlled-access roadway within their respective jurisdictions by any class or kind of traffic that is found to be incompatible with the normal and safe movement of traffic.
>
> B. The state transportation commission or the local authority adopting any such prohibition shall erect and maintain official traffic-control devices on the controlled-access roadway on which the prohibitions are applicable, and, when in place, no person shall disobey the restrictions stated on the devices.

**What it means:** No statute bans pedestrians from every New Mexico freeway. Where a sign bans pedestrians, you must stay off. Stand at the start of the on-ramp, before any such sign, or at a truck stop.

### NMSA 1978, § 66-8-116: Penalty assessment misdemeanors (schedule)

**Source:** [New Mexico Legislature, 2025 S.B. 265 (introduced), § 4](https://www.nmlegis.gov/Sessions/25%20Regular/bills/senate/SB0265.html). The bill reprints the existing schedule, with proposed increases shown as bracketed deletions and underlined insertions. The quote below is the existing (bracketed) amounts. S.B. 265 died. Later bills that would also have raised these amounts (2025 S.B. 225, 2026 S.B. 214) also died.

> A. As used in the Motor Vehicle Code and the Boat Act, "penalty assessment misdemeanor" means violation of any of the following listed sections of the NMSA 1978 for which, except as provided in Subsections D through F of this section, the listed penalty assessment is established:
> [...]
> COMMON NAME OF OFFENSE / SECTION VIOLATED / PENALTY ASSESSMENT
> [...]
> Controlled access violation / 66-7-321 / 25.00
> [...]
> Pedestrian violation / 66-7-333 through 66-7-340 / 25.00

**What it means:** Soliciting a ride from the roadway (§ 66-7-340), walking on the wrong side (§ 66-7-339) and ignoring a freeway pedestrian ban (§ 66-7-321) each carry a $25 penalty assessment, plus court fees.
sections.history:
### 2024 special session: "Unsafe Use of Public Highways and Medians Act" (died)

**Source:** [2024 (1st Special Session) S.B. 11](https://www.nmlegis.gov/Sessions/24%20Special/bills/senate/SB0011.HTML) and its [bill status page](https://www.nmlegis.gov/Legislation/Legislation?chamber=S&legType=B&legNo=11&year=24s) ("Died")

The bill would have made it unlawful for a pedestrian to "occupy a travel lane of the exit or entrance ramp of a highway". It would also have banned walking on any highway with a posted speed limit of 30 mph or more. It died. Neither rule is law.

jurisdictions.title: Texas (US-TX)
jurisdictions.statusLine: Restricted. You may not stand *in a roadway* to solicit a ride. The roadway does not include the shoulder, so thumbing from the shoulder or curb is not covered by this rule. Pedestrians can be banned from controlled-access highways where signs are posted.

sections.summary:
Texas follows the standard Uniform Vehicle Code rule: "A person may not stand in a roadway to solicit a ride." Texas defines "roadway" as the part of the highway used for travel, "other than the berm or shoulder". Standing on the shoulder, the curb or the sidewalk to hitchhike is therefore not banned by state law. Standing in a travel lane is.

What applies to hitchhikers:

- **Stay out of the travel lanes.** Standing in the roadway to solicit a ride is a misdemeanor punishable by a fine of $1 to $200.
- **Freeways:** the Texas Transportation Commission (on state highways) and cities or counties (on their own roads) may ban pedestrians from limited-access or controlled-access highways. The ban applies where official signs are posted, so check the signs at your spot.
- **Walk on the sidewalk** if there is one. Otherwise walk on the left side of the road or shoulder, facing traffic.
sections.laws:
### Tex. Transp. Code § 552.007: Solicitation by pedestrians

**Source:** [Texas Legislative Council, Transportation Code ch. 552](https://tcss.legis.texas.gov/resources/TN/htm/TN.552.htm) (official statute text, file last modified April 2026; section unchanged since Acts 1995, 74th Leg., ch. 165)

> (a) A person may not stand in a roadway to solicit a ride, contribution, employment, or business from an occupant of a vehicle, except that a person may stand in a roadway to solicit a charitable contribution if authorized to do so by the local authority having jurisdiction over the roadway.
>
> (b) A person may not stand on or near a highway to solicit the watching or guarding of a vehicle parked or to be parked on the highway.

**What it means:** Don't step into the lanes to ask for a ride. The rule covers only the "roadway", and Texas law excludes the shoulder from the roadway (see § 541.302 below). Standing on the shoulder or curb with a sign or your thumb out is not prohibited by this section. Make sure a driver can pull fully off the road to pick you up.

### Tex. Transp. Code § 552.0071(g): Roadway for charity solicitation

**Source:** [Texas Legislative Council, Transportation Code ch. 552](https://tcss.legis.texas.gov/resources/TN/htm/TN.552.htm)

> (g) For purposes of a solicitation under Subsection (a), a roadway is defined to include the roadbed, shoulder, median, curbs, safety zones, sidewalks, and utility easements located adjacent to or near the roadway.

**What it means:** This broader "roadway" definition applies only to local permits for charity collections (such as firefighters' boot drives). It does not change the general definition that applies to ride solicitation.

### Tex. Transp. Code § 541.302: Traffic areas (definitions)

**Source:** [Texas Legislative Council, Transportation Code ch. 541](https://tcss.legis.texas.gov/resources/TN/htm/TN.541.htm)

> (5) "Highway or street" means the width between the boundary lines of a publicly maintained way any part of which is open to the public for vehicular travel.
> [...]
> (11) "Roadway" means the portion of a highway, other than the berm or shoulder, that is improved, designed, or ordinarily used for vehicular travel. If a highway includes at least two separate roadways, the term applies to each roadway separately.
> [...]
> (15) "Shoulder" means the portion of a highway that is: (A) adjacent to the roadway; (B) designed or ordinarily used for parking; (C) distinguished from the roadway by different design, construction, or marking; and (D) not intended for normal vehicular travel.

**What it means:** The shoulder is part of the "highway" but not the "roadway". The ride-solicitation ban in § 552.007(a) covers only the roadway.

### Tex. Transp. Code § 552.006: Use of sidewalk

**Source:** [Texas Legislative Council, Transportation Code ch. 552](https://tcss.legis.texas.gov/resources/TN/htm/TN.552.htm) (last amended by Acts 2023, 88th Leg., R.S., Ch. 815 (H.B. 1277), eff. September 1, 2023)

> (a) A pedestrian may not walk along and on a roadway if an adjacent sidewalk is provided and is accessible to the pedestrian.
>
> (b) If a sidewalk is not provided, a pedestrian walking along and on a highway shall walk on the left side of the roadway or the shoulder of the highway facing oncoming traffic, unless the left side of the roadway or the shoulder of the highway facing oncoming traffic is obstructed or unsafe.

**What it means:** Use the sidewalk where there is one. Otherwise walk facing traffic on the left side of the road or shoulder.

### Tex. Transp. Code § 545.065: State and local regulation of limited-access or controlled-access highways

**Source:** [Texas Legislative Council, Transportation Code ch. 545](https://tcss.legis.texas.gov/resources/TN/htm/TN.545.htm)

> (a) The Texas Transportation Commission by resolution or order recorded in its minutes may prohibit the use of a limited-access or controlled-access highway under the jurisdiction of the commission by a parade, funeral procession, pedestrian, bicycle, electric bicycle, motorcycle equipped with a motor that has an engine piston displacement of 250 cubic centimeters or less, or nonmotorized traffic.
>
> (b) If the commission adopts a rule under Subsection (a), the commission shall erect and maintain official traffic-control devices on the portions of the limited-access or controlled-access highway to which the rule applies.
>
> (c) A local authority by ordinance may prohibit the use of a limited-access or controlled-access roadway under the jurisdiction of the authority by a parade, funeral procession, pedestrian, bicycle, electric bicycle, motorcycle equipped with a motor that has an engine piston displacement of 250 cubic centimeters or less, or nonmotorized traffic.
>
> (d) If a local authority adopts an ordinance under Subsection (c), the authority shall erect and maintain official traffic-control devices on the portions of the limited-access or controlled-access roadway to which the ordinance applies.

**What it means:** No statute bans pedestrians from every Texas freeway. The state or a city can ban them on a particular freeway, and the ban is marked by signs. If you see a "pedestrians prohibited" sign at a ramp, stand before the sign, not past it. Frontage roads are not part of the freeway itself.

### Tex. Transp. Code §§ 542.301 and 542.401: Offense and penalty

**Source:** [Texas Legislative Council, Transportation Code ch. 542](https://tcss.legis.texas.gov/resources/TN/htm/TN.542.htm)

> Sec. 542.301. GENERAL OFFENSE. (a) A person commits an offense if the person performs an act prohibited or fails to perform an act required by this subtitle. (b) Except as otherwise provided, an offense under this subtitle is a misdemeanor.
>
> Sec. 542.401. GENERAL PENALTY. A person convicted of an offense that is a misdemeanor under this subtitle for which another penalty is not provided shall be punished by a fine of not less than $1 or more than $200.

**What it means:** Soliciting a ride from the roadway, or walking on a posted freeway, is a fine-only misdemeanor of $1 to $200, plus court costs.
